_comment: Pre-registered per-fault target-metric panel (fault_catalog.md §6 realized). For each fault, the Prometheus signal(s) that MUST move if the injection actually took effect. verify_injection.py evaluates these over the baseline vs injection windows and writes a confirmed|borderline|unconfirmed verdict. One target per fault is marked canonical=true (drives the verdict); others are corroborating. Direction: 'increase'|'decrease'. threshold_sigma = min standardized delta over baseline stdev; min_fraction = min share of the injection window past the raw threshold. These are QC gates, NOT the study's modality claims (those live in fault_catalog.md). | 5 Sept 2026: entries for the ten new fault families added, every threshold MEASURED with faults/measure_targets.sh on both applications rather than written from the mechanism. Two calibration passes were needed: the first found cAdvisor's process metric group disabled by default, the second found those same metrics reading 0.0000 without pid:host. A metric that exists and is always zero is more dangerous than one that is missing.

_windows._settle_note: skip the first 30s of the injection window when scoring: 1m-rate-windowed metrics take ~a rate-window to ramp after onset. Campaign runs should use INJECTION_S >= 120 so a clean settled segment remains.

_metric_naming: CALIBRATED 2026-07-28 against the live stack. Request-duration metric name differs by service runtime: Go/Node services (catalogue, frontend) expose 'http_request_duration_seconds'; Java/Spring services (cart, orders, payment, user, shipping) expose 'request_duration_seconds'. Prometheus job labels are singular for carts ('cart'). cAdvisor container 'name' labels are 'docker-compose_<svc>_1'; carts=docker-compose_carts_1 (regex '.*carts_1$' excludes carts-db). NOTE: this cAdvisor build exposes NO cfs-throttle metric, so svc_cpu_cap verifies via app latency, not throttle counters.

slow_db_catalogue.name: catalogue_p95_latency
slow_db_catalogue.why: added DB latency inflates catalogue request duration; DB container metrics stay flat (blind spot)

error_storm_catalogue.name: catalogue_5xx_rate
error_storm_catalogue.why: broken DB connections surface as 5xx on catalogue-backed routes

svc_cpu_cap_carts.name: carts_p95_latency
svc_cpu_cap_carts.why: throttled service serves requests slower (this cadvisor build has no cfs-throttle metric, so latency is the QC signal)

svc_cpu_cap_carts.name: carts_cpu_usage_capped
svc_cpu_cap_carts.why: usage pinned at/below the imposed quota

svc_mem_cap_carts.name: carts_memory_limit_dropped
svc_mem_cap_carts.why: the cap is applied: limit drops from host-total (~42GB) to the cap (<=300MB). Reliable for both intensities. (usage/limit ratio is unusable: uncapped baseline limit = host total.) carts working set is ~545MB, so any cap <=300MB necessarily constrains it.

svc_mem_cap_carts.name: carts_oom_kills
svc_mem_cap_carts.why: aggressive cap (160MB, below the working set) forces OOM kills; subtle cap causes GC pressure without necessarily OOMing

dependency_outage_payment.name: payment_cpu_drops
dependency_outage_payment.why:
MEASURED 5 Sept on campaign run r1: payment CPU 0.00316 -> 0.000603 cores, direction correct, 95% of injection samples past the threshold. Read `borderline` on sigma alone.
The 2-sigma gate is UNSATISFIABLE: baseline 0.00316 with std 0.00197, so -2 sigma demands -0.0008 cores. CPU cannot be negative. A paused container's CPU can only fall to zero, which for this metric is barely 1.6 sigma away from where it starts. Lowered to 1.0 - a reachable gate. The coverage test is doing the real work here, and it is the right test: the container is paused, so its CPU should sit at the floor for essentially the whole window, which is what 95% coverage says.
METRICS-WEAK fault (calibrated: payment baseline CPU ~0.004 core drops ~58% to ~0.0018 under pause, smeared by the 1m rate window; may verify BORDERLINE). This aligns with fault_catalog.md: TRACES win this fault (the broken orders->payment edge), not metrics. See orders_5xx note below.

dependency_outage_payment.name: orders_5xx_rate_EXPECTED_BLIND
dependency_outage_payment.why: CALIBRATION FINDING: stays ~0. docker pause FREEZES payment, so orders' HTTP call HANGS (blocked socket read) rather than fail-fast - the request never completes with an error status inside the window. A frozen dependency is metrics/logs-INVISIBLE while the kernel sees orders threads blocked in read() on the payment socket. This is a concrete instance of the study's kernel-wins thesis; kept as documentation, not a verification gate.

queue_backlog.name: queue_master_cpu_drops
queue_backlog.why: calibrated: queue-master baseline CPU ~0.008 core drops ~77% to ~0.0019 under pause (1m-rate-smeared). METRICS-WEAK silent-failure fault: orders keep succeeding, no error anywhere; the real signal is the KERNEL (queue-master cgroup goes quiet while rabbitmq keeps taking inbound) - matches fault_catalog.md's kernel-wins prediction.

noisy_neighbor.name: neighbor_cpu_active
noisy_neighbor.why: CALIBRATED & PREMISE VALIDATED (subtle, 1.0-cpu cap): neighbor consumes ~0.75 core (fired; host CPU 28%->45%) while service KPIs stay within normal variance - carts p95 21.8ms->23.1ms (+6%), catalogue p95 4.75ms->4.75ms (0%). The kernel-only showcase: CPU contention is host/kernel-visible but app-metric-blind. This target verifies the fault FIRED; the KPIs-stay-flat premise is the study finding, not a verification gate.

anomaly_disk.name: host_disk_write_ops
anomaly_disk.why: MEASURED 5 Sept during campaign run anomaly_disk_r5: 578 -> 2058 writes/s (3.56x). Replaces rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total[1m]), which failed on all five repeats with a ratio of 0.95x - not because the fault was weak but because io_time is a UTILISATION metric and utilisation was already spoken for. LTTng writes the kernel trace continuously throughout every run at ~53 MB/s, which is exactly the measured baseline of node_disk_written_bytes_total, so the disk is near-saturated before the fault starts and 'fraction of time busy' has nowhere left to climb. Unbounded counters - operations, bytes, queue depth - show the fault plainly.

anomaly_disk.name: host_disk_queue_depth
anomaly_disk.why: MEASURED: 5.49 -> 12.95 (2.36x). Weighted io_time is queue depth x time, so unlike plain io_time it keeps rising after the device is already busy.

anomaly_disk.name: host_disk_write_bytes
anomaly_disk.why: MEASURED: 53.3 -> 133.4 MB/s (2.50x). The 53.3 MB/s baseline is the kernel trace itself.

anomaly_mem.name: host_mem_available_drop
anomaly_mem.why: MEASURED 5 Sept on campaign run anomaly_mem_r1: available goes 0.79 -> 0.40 (33.7 GB -> 19.9 GB), sigma -14.6. The previous entry demanded < 0.25 and its own comment said 'Finalize on VM calibration' - nobody did, and 0.25 is unreachable: stress-ng vm-hang asks for 88% of RAM but MemAvailable bottoms out near 0.40. All four collected repeats read unconfirmed on fraction alone, with direction correct and sigma at -14.6. min_fraction is 0.5 rather than 0.8 because the allocation RAMPS - the first part of the injection window is still filling, so early samples legitimately sit above any floor. A threshold that assumes a step change cannot score a fault that ramps.

anomaly_mem.name: host_major_page_faults
anomaly_mem.why: MEASURED: 0 -> 73/s. The system is genuinely short of memory and going to disk for pages, which is the consequence that matters rather than the allocation itself.

anomaly_net.name: catalogue_p95_latency_net
anomaly_net.why: CALIBRATED (wave-2): host-bridge netem (100ms delay + 3% loss on br-<compose>) inflates every inter-service hop; catalogue p95 (front-end->catalogue->DB) rises. node-NIC throughput is NOT a reliable signal for added latency (internal bridge traffic doesn't traverse the physical NIC).

svc_net_carts.name: carts_p95_latency
svc_net_carts.why: per-container netem inside carts' netns inflates carts request latency; single-service impairment (front-end sees it upstream). Calibrate on the VM.

lock_contention.name: lock_contention_threads
lock_contention.why: MEASURED 5 Sept: 17 threads on both applications, and the series does not exist before injection, so the baseline is 0. A co-located workload fault is confirmed by the workload being there and doing its characteristic thing; the contention itself is a kernel claim, not a metrics one.

lock_contention.name: lock_contention_cpu
lock_contention.why: MEASURED: 1.03 cores Sock Shop, 0.95 Train Ticket, against a 1.0 cap.

priority_inversion.name: priority_inversion_cpu
priority_inversion.why: MEASURED: 1.03 cores Sock Shop, 0.98 Train Ticket. The inversion itself is only visible in the wait times the workload reports and in the kernel stream.

deadlock.name: deadlock_threads
deadlock.why: MEASURED: 25 threads on both applications. CPU is deliberately NOT a target here - it reads 0.0001, because deadlocked threads consume nothing. That is the fault's whole character and the reason it is hard: a stuck system looks like an idle one.

fd_exhaustion.name: front_end_fd_ceiling
fd_exhaustion.why: The cap is set to a fraction of what the service is using at inject time, so the descriptor count is forced DOWN and then pinned. MEASURED on Train Ticket: 305 in use, capped to 183, count fell to 257. Deliberately has no abs_threshold - the absolute number depends entirely on the service (21 idle on Sock Shop's Node front-end, 175 on Train Ticket's JVM gateway), so only the direction and the sigma are portable.

conn_pool_exhaustion.name: db_sockets_held
conn_pool_exhaustion.why: MEASURED 5 Sept: 4 -> 154 sockets on Sock Shop (38.5x) and 204 -> 2005 on Train Ticket (9.8x). The strongest signal of the whole panel, and it comes from the server rather than from the holder.

resource_abuse.name: resource_abuse_cpu
resource_abuse.why: MEASURED: 1.01 cores Sock Shop, 0.97 Train Ticket. Volume of CPU is the only thing metrics can see; whether it is ABUSE rather than work is the question the study asks, and no metric answers it.

data_exfiltration.name: exfil_bytes_out
data_exfiltration.why: MEASURED 5 Sept: 42.0 MB/s on both applications. This read 0.0000 until the recipe was changed to send to a separate sink container - the first version sent to 127.0.0.1 inside its own container, so 839 MB crossed no interface and no counter saw it.

data_exfiltration.name: exfil_bytes_in_at_sink
data_exfiltration.why: MEASURED: 41.7 MB/s Sock Shop, 42.0 Train Ticket. The receiving end, on purpose - the sender's own claim was 839 MB and was true while nothing left the container.

fork_storm.name: fork_storm_processes
fork_storm.why: MEASURED: 201 processes on both applications. Per-container rather than host-wide, which matters: node_forks_total is 12.2x on Sock Shop but only 7.2x on Train Ticket, and in an earlier pass 1.05x, because TT already forks ~112/s from 40 JVMs and Nacos health checks. A host counter cannot serve both applications; this one does.

fork_storm.name: host_fork_rate
fork_storm.why: MEASURED: 8.7 -> 106.5/s Sock Shop (12.2x), 15.7 -> 113.1 Train Ticket (7.2x). Corroborating only - see above for why it cannot be canonical.

nagle_delayed_ack.name: nagle_workload_present
nagle_delayed_ack.why: MEASURED: 1.00 cores on both. This is a PRESENCE check and nothing more. The fault's actual signature - a ~99 ms stall clustered within 1 ms of itself, against a TCP_NODELAY control at 0.51 ms in the same run - is invisible to every metric we collect, which is precisely why the family is in the catalogue.

dns_delay.name: dns_delay_no_metric_signature
dns_delay.why: REGISTERED AS A KNOWN NEGATIVE. Two calibration passes found nothing that moves: host UDP counters 1.00x, front-end receive rate 0.58-0.83x (down, not up). The fault is real - the iptables rule drops 24 queries while the app runs, wall-clock time goes 914 ms -> 20,034 ms and 31 of 400 requests fail - but p50 reads 3.9 ms and p95 8.0 ms, BOTH BETTER than baseline. It hides in the tail, where no aggregate metric looks. Expect this check to fail; the failure is the finding, and verify_injection will report borderline rather than silently passing.
